title: Evidence-grounded large language models guide perovskite solar cell design and optimization
authors: YanKai Chen, Zhi Wan, ZiHao Li, Tao Jing
abstract: Using large language models to interpret experimental evidence, design discriminating experiments and formulate well-supported mechanistic explanations remains a central challenge in materials research. Here we establish PSM-Bench, an 800-question benchmark developed by perovskite researchers to evaluate scientific reasoning in perovskite photovoltaics. We also introduce OpenPerov, an expert-informed language-model framework that learns from expert-calibrated evidence records reconstructed from 4,532 articles; these records link experimental strategies, controls and observations to mechanistic interpretations. Structured-evidence adaptation outperformed conventional question-answer training, and OpenPerov Flash ranked first among 13 closed-book systems. OpenPerov Pro raised Scientific Mastery further, from 87.6 to 89.1, by revising selected passages with retrieved evidence. On questions derived from subsequent studies, both models also outscored expert-authored answers. In an experimental test of self-assembled monolayer design, OpenPerov selected a K analogue that outperformed the Na analogue preferred by experts. Devices incorporating the selected contact reached a power conversion efficiency of 27.05% and retained 96.74% of their steady-state reference efficiency after 1,000 h of dark thermal ageing at 85 $^\circ$C. These results show that reconstructed scientific reasoning provides an effective basis for building domain models that interpret experiments and inform materials design.

infographic.key_insight: Training language models on structured experimental evidence helped OpenPerov reason about perovskite solar cells and select a contact material that outperformed an expert-preferred alternative.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Evidence-grounded AI could guide interface-material selection and experimental design for more efficient, thermally stable perovskite solar cells.
method: Reconstruct expert-calibrated evidence records from 4,532 articles.
Adapt models using linked strategies, controls, observations and mechanistic interpretations.
Refine selected responses with retrieved evidence and experimentally test a self-assembled monolayer choice.
infographic.evidence_signal: On the 800-question PSM-Bench, OpenPerov Flash led 13 closed-book systems; the selected K-analogue contact enabled 27.05% efficiency and 96.74% retention after 1,000 h of dark thermal ageing at 85 °C.
infographic.watch_item: The reported dark thermal ageing test does not establish durability under illumination or outdoor operating conditions.
infographic.paper_title: Evidence-grounded large language models guide perovskite solar cell design and optimization

title: Synergistic Graphene and PEDOT:PSS Layers on Silicon for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability in Schottky Junction Solar Cells
authors: Kentaro Nakajo, Hojun Im, Keiichiro Nishimura, Masahiro Teraoka, Masaya Kikuchi
abstract: While graphene/n-type silicon (Gr/n-Si) and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si solar cells offer a cost-effective alternative to conventional photovoltaics, achieving simultaneous high power conversion efficiency (PCE) and long-term environmental stability remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report the synergistic enhancement of both performance and stability in a planar trilayer PEDOT:PSS/Gr/n-Si Schottky junction architecture. By systematically benchmarking this hybrid device against pristine Gr/n-Si and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si reference cells fabricated on untextured substrates, we isolate the fundamental optoelectronic and barrier functions of the carbon lattice. Comprehensive analyses reveal that the PEDOT:PSS layer simultaneously functions as an anti-reflection coating, a moderate p-type dopant for the underlying graphene, and a conductivity enhancer, collectively optimizing interfacial charge transport. Consequently, the trilayer device achieves a PCE of 8.52%, markedly outperforming the pristine Gr/n-Si reference cell (4.56%). Crucially, the atomic impermeability of the graphene sheet serves as a robust environmental barrier. While bare PEDOT:PSS/n-Si junctions retained only ~29% of their initial efficiency after 75 days of ambient exposure, graphene shields the active junction from moisture-induced degradation of the hygroscopic PEDOT:PSS overlayer. This enables the trilayer device to retain approximately 90% of its initial efficiency over the same 75-day period. The complementary roles of graphene as both a highly crystalline charge transport interface and an impermeable protective barrier establish a highly effective strategy for engineering high-efficiency, environmentally stable hybrid photovoltaics.

infographic.key_insight: A PEDOT:PSS/graphene/n-silicon trilayer combines improved solar-cell efficiency with graphene-enabled protection against environmental degradation.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The planar hybrid architecture offers a route to more efficient, durable silicon Schottky solar cells without substrate texturing.
method: Benchmark trilayer devices against graphene/n-Si and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si reference cells on untextured substrates.
Use PEDOT:PSS for anti-reflection, moderate graphene p-doping, and enhanced conductivity.
Use graphene as a charge-transport interface and moisture barrier.
infographic.evidence_signal: The trilayer achieved 8.52% power conversion efficiency versus 4.56% for graphene/n-Si, retaining approximately 90% of its initial efficiency after 75 days in ambient conditions versus approximately 29% for PEDOT:PSS/n-Si.
infographic.watch_item: The reported 75-day ambient test does not establish long-term outdoor durability or scalability of defect-free graphene barriers.
infographic.paper_title: Synergistic Graphene and PEDOT:PSS Layers on Silicon for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability in Schottky Junction Solar Cells

title: Stable AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for thin film tandem photovoltaics
authors: Shiling Dong, Yongjie Wang, Hae-Jun Seok, Mengyuan Huang, Edward Newton, Der Ying Chen
abstract: AgBiS2 has rapidly risen in efficiency as single-junction photovoltaics (PVs), but its potential for tandem PVs is unexplored. Herein, we perform optical modeling based on the experimental absorption spectrum of AgBiS2, revealing that, as the NIR sub-cell, efficiencies exceeding 47.9% are achievable in triple-junction tandems, superseding tandems using Pb/Sn perovskite NIR cells (35.9%). However, fulfilling this potential requires overcoming the limited transport properties of AgBiS2 nanocrystal films, which constrains film thicknesses to only 30-50 nm, severely restricting NIR response. A solution-phase ligand exchange process is herein developed, allowing one-step deposition of passivated AgBiS2 nanocrystals that maintain efficient charge-carrier extraction despite an order of magnitude increase in film thickness. These films enable 24.0%-efficient four-terminal tandems with visible-light-absorbing lead-halide perovskite sub-cells, and monolithic tandems successfully demonstrating voltage addition. AgBiS2 PVs have high stability, retaining >90% of the original efficiency after 3 months of storage in dry air without encapsulation. This work establishes the significant potential of AgBiS2 as a stable and scalable NIR absorber for tandem PVs.

infographic.key_insight: Solution-phase ligand exchange enables thicker AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers, supporting demonstrated 24.0%-efficient four-terminal tandems with perovskite sub-cells.
infographic.engineering_relevance: One-step deposition of passivated AgBiS2 nanocrystals offers a route toward scalable, stable near-infrared sub-cells for thin-film tandem photovoltaics.
method: Model tandem performance using the experimental AgBiS2 absorption spectrum.
Apply solution-phase ligand exchange to preserve charge extraction in thicker nanocrystal films.
Integrate AgBiS2 with visible-absorbing perovskites in four-terminal and monolithic tandems.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports 24.0% four-terminal tandem efficiency, voltage addition in monolithic tandems, and >90% efficiency retention after three months of unencapsulated dry-air storage; triple-junction efficiencies above 47.9% are modeled, not demonstrated.
infographic.watch_item: Dry-air storage stability does not establish operational durability under illumination, heat, or humidity.
infographic.paper_title: Stable AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for thin film tandem photovoltaics

title: High-Entropy A-Site Disorder Enhances Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity and Stability in Nickelate Thin Films
authors: Min-Ju Choi, Le Wang, Krishna Prasad Koirala, Hyoju Park, Mark E. Bowden, Elizabeth Helen Krenkel
abstract: Rare-earth nickelates are among the most active oxide electrocatalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), owing to their tunable Ni-O covalency, near-unity eg occupancy, and sensitivity to A-site chemistry, oxygen stoichiometry, and epitaxial strain. Here, we use epitaxial A-site high-entropy (La0.2Pr0.2Nd0.2Sm0.2Eu0.2)NiO3 thin films to reveal how epitaxial strain influences defect formation, Ni valence, electronic structure, and OER activity in a chemically disordered rare-earth (RE) sublattice. Tensile strain promotes Ruddlesden-Popper fault formation, interrupts the corner-sharing NiO6 network, and lowers the average Ni oxidation state. Although the occupied density of states near the Fermi level remains largely unchanged, O K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy reveals increased low-energy unoccupied states under tensile strain. First-principles calculations suggest that tensile strain shifts RE 4f-derived states toward the Fermi level, enhancing RE 4f-O 2p-Ni 3d hybridization. These coupled structural and electronic changes lead to earlier OER onset, stronger pre-catalytic Ni redox features, and higher activity than compressively strained films and representative single-A-site nickelates. The high-entropy nickelate also shows enhanced resistance to OER-induced structural degradation compared with LaNiO3. These results suggest that A-site configurational disorder and epitaxial strain can jointly tune defect formation and rare-earth-derived electronic states, providing a route for improving perovskite oxide electrocatalysts.

infographic.key_insight: A-site high-entropy disorder and tensile strain jointly improve oxygen evolution activity in nickelate thin films, while the high-entropy composition enhances structural stability relative to LaNiO3.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This work offers a materials-design route for perovskite oxide water-splitting electrocatalysts, rather than solar cells or AI systems.
method: Study epitaxial (La0.2Pr0.2Nd0.2Sm0.2Eu0.2)NiO3 films under different strain conditions.
Probe structural defects, Ni valence, and electronic states using spectroscopy and structural characterization.
Combine first-principles calculations with OER activity and degradation comparisons.
infographic.evidence_signal: Tensile-strained films exhibit earlier OER onset, stronger pre-catalytic Ni redox features, and higher activity than compressively strained films and representative single-A-site nickelates; the high-entropy nickelate also resists structural degradation better than LaNiO3.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative activity or durability metrics, and transfer from epitaxial thin films to practical electrodes remains unestablished.
infographic.paper_title: High-Entropy A-Site Disorder Enhances Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity and Stability in Nickelate Thin Films

title: Multiwavelength Photoluminescence as a Non-destructive Probe of Depth-Dependent UV Damage in Perovskite Semiconductors
authors: Zixu Huang, Julisa Juarez, Akash Dasgupta, David S. Ginger
abstract: Buried interfaces play a critical role in the operational stability of perovskite optoelectronic devices, yet remain challenging to probe non-destructively. Here, we demonstrate a multiwavelength photoluminescence-based approach exploiting the wavelength-dependent absorption of perovskites, enabling fast, and non-destructive probing of depth-sensitive degradation behavior of perovskite devices under operational conditions. Using ultraviolet (UV) light-soaking with different indium tin oxide (ITO) modifiers as a test case, we employ wide-field photoluminescence (PL) imaging, time-resolved photoluminescence (trPL) and ideality factor measurements with different wavelength excitation to characterize degradation behavior of both perovskite thin films and photovoltaic devices under UV soaking. Using only nondestructive characterization, we show that UV-induced degradation in p-i-n perovskite solar cells occurs preferentially at the HTL interface, adversely affecting device stability, consistent with ex-situ destructive tests. Our results also show that modifying the buried interface with 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane reduces UV-induced damage at the buried interface, thus improving the UV stability of both perovskite films and devices. This work establishes a fast, non-destructive strategy to screen depth-dependent degradation in perovskite devices, offering insights for interface design and stability optimization.

infographic.key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence non-destructively reveals depth-dependent UV damage concentrated near the buried hole-transport-layer interface in p-i-n perovskite solar cells.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Depth-sensitive optical screening can guide interface design, with 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane modification reducing buried-interface damage and improving UV stability.
method: Use wavelength-dependent absorption to probe different depths.
Combine wide-field PL imaging, time-resolved PL and ideality-factor measurements under UV soaking.
Compare perovskite films and devices with different ITO modifiers.
infographic.evidence_signal: Non-destructive measurements localized preferential degradation at the hole-transport-layer interface, consistent with ex-situ destructive tests, and showed improved UV stability with interface modification.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative stability gains or evidence that UV-soaking results generalize to long-term operation under combined stressors.
infographic.paper_title: Multiwavelength Photoluminescence as a Non-destructive Probe of Depth-Dependent UV Damage in Perovskite Semiconductors

title: Provenance-grouped protocol for evaluating machine learning in perovskite photovoltaics
authors: Qiwei Han, Chi Zhou
abstract: Machine-learning models for perovskite solar cells are typically evaluated using random data splits, which we show systematically leak information through massive internal duplication. Because nearly two-thirds of curated devices share their exact recipe with another, random splits primarily reward the mere recall of historical data rather than testing true physical generalisation. To solve this, we mapped the institutional provenance of the Perovskite Database and established a rigorous hierarchy of grouped splits that progressively isolate duplicate devices, publications, and institutions. Benchmarking thirteen models establishes new state-of-the-art performance across all splits and reveals a critical regime shift: while tree ensembles dominate random splits by recognising familiar recipes, their ranking collapses on genuinely unseen institutions and future discoveries, where composition-aware neural architectures excel. Furthermore, feature importance demonstrates that the device architecture and fabrication methodology dictate final efficiency just as strongly as the absorber chemistry. This standardised protocol empowers the community to separate memorisation from true physical discovery.

infographic.key_insight: Random data splits can reward recipe memorisation, while provenance-grouped evaluation reveals which models generalise to unseen perovskite solar-cell research.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Reliable device optimisation requires models that account for architecture and fabrication as well as absorber chemistry.
method: Map institutional provenance in the Perovskite Database.
Apply grouped splits that progressively isolate duplicate devices, publications and institutions.
Benchmark 13 models and analyse feature importance.
infographic.evidence_signal: Nearly two-thirds of curated devices share an exact recipe with another; tree ensembles lead on random splits, while composition-aware neural models excel on unseen institutions and future discoveries.
infographic.watch_item: Implementation depends on reliable recipe and provenance metadata, and the abstract provides no numerical performance margins.
infographic.paper_title: Provenance-grouped protocol for evaluating machine learning in perovskite photovoltaics

title: Amorphous selenium-alloyed TeOx thin-film solar cells
authors: Zhaoheng Ling, Linqu Luo, Chrysa Aivalioti, Temur Maksudov, Mengxi Zhang, Theodoulos Kalogerakis
abstract: Tellurium dioxide (TeO$_2$) is a wide-bandgap oxide with attractive processing versatility and emerging p-type semiconducting behaviour, making it a promising material system for optoelectronic and photovoltaic applications. However, TeO$_2$-derived thin films prepared by scalable manufacturing processes, such as vacuum sublimation, can contain residual metallic Te$^0$ species that introduce trap states, limit hole transport, and promote carrier recombination. Here, we demonstrate a selenium alloying strategy to control the defect chemistry of vacuum-sublimed TeO$_x$ films. TeO$_2$:Se powder mixtures (90:10~wt\%) were thermally evaporated and subsequently annealed in air at 225~$^\circ$C for up to 9~h, yielding amorphous TeO$_x$:Se films with an optical bandgap of 0.98~eV under optimised conditions. Structural, chemical, optical, and electrical analyses show that prolonged annealing promotes Se redistribution, suppresses residual Te$^0$ to approximately 0.4\%, reduces the film's surface roughness, and shifts the valence-band edge. To evaluate the potential of TeO$_x$:Se for photovoltaic applications, we fabricated thin-film solar cells with an ITO/ZnO/TeO$_x$:Se/MoO$_x$/Ag architecture. Devices based on an 80~nm TeO$_x$:Se active layer annealed for 9~h exhibit optimal performance, with broadband photocurrent generation from 300 to 1000~nm, yielding an open-circuit voltage of 0.50~V, a short-circuit current density of 8.50~mA~cm$^{-2}$, a fill factor of 0.44, and a maximum power conversion efficiency of approximately 1.87\%. These results establish selenium-alloyed TeO$_x$ as a viable oxide-derived absorber for thin-film photovoltaics and highlight chemical-state control as an effective route for improving photovoltaic performance.

infographic.key_insight: Selenium alloying and air annealing suppress residual metallic tellurium in amorphous TeOx films, enabling thin-film solar cells with approximately 1.87% peak efficiency.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Chemical-state control offers a route to improving oxide-derived photovoltaic absorbers made by scalable vacuum deposition.
method: Thermally evaporate a 90:10 wt% TeO2:Se powder mixture.
Anneal films in air at 225 °C for up to 9 hours.
Integrate the absorber into ITO/ZnO/TeOx:Se/MoOx/Ag solar cells.
infographic.evidence_signal: The optimal 80 nm absorber annealed for 9 hours yielded 0.50 V open-circuit voltage, 8.50 mA/cm² short-circuit current density, 0.44 fill factor, and photocurrent response across 300–1000 nm; prolonged annealing reduced residual metallic Te to approximately 0.4%.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract does not report long-term stability or large-area device performance, and the 9-hour anneal may constrain manufacturing throughput.
infographic.paper_title: Amorphous selenium-alloyed TeOx thin-film solar cells

title: Controlling Surface Chemistry in Tin-Lead Perovskites for High-Efficiency Solar Cells
authors: Lijun Chen, Sitong Zhao, Gaukhar Nigmetova, David Garcia Romero, Matteo Pitaro, Sofia Lerda
abstract: Interfacial nonradiative recombination limits tin-lead perovskite photovoltaics. Here we show that neutral ethylenediamine chelates undercoordinated metals at tin-rich surfaces, weakens metal-iodide bonds, and removes excess tin, reconstructing the surface towards a stoichiometric tin-to-lead ratio. In contrast, protonated ethylenediammonium iodide initially passivates undercoordinated metal sites before undergoing defect-assisted deprotonation. Atomistic simulations reveal that subsurface iodide vacancies promote iodide migration and lower the energetic cost of deprotonation. Ethylenediamine-induced reconstruction produces stronger n-type surface character, facilitates electron extraction into C60, and suppresses interfacial nonradiative recombination, enabling methylammonium-free solar cells with a power conversion efficiency of 25.86%. Together, these distinct surface reaction pathways and the defect-assisted evolution of the passivating species underscore the importance of understanding perovskite surface chemistry for the rational design of molecular passivation strategies.

infographic.key_insight: Neutral ethylenediamine removes excess surface tin and restores tin–lead stoichiometry, improving electron extraction and reducing interfacial recombination.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Controlling molecular protonation and surface defects offers a route to more efficient methylammonium-free tin–lead perovskite solar cells.
method: Compare neutral ethylenediamine with protonated ethylenediammonium iodide passivation.
Use atomistic simulations to examine vacancy-assisted iodide migration and deprotonation.
Link surface reconstruction to electronic character, C60 electron extraction, and device performance.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports 25.86% power conversion efficiency and simulations showing that subsurface iodide vacancies lower the energetic cost of deprotonation.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract does not establish long-term operational stability or manufacturing-scale reproducibility of the surface treatment.
infographic.paper_title: Controlling Surface Chemistry in Tin-Lead Perovskites for High-Efficiency Solar Cells

title: Diffusion-Based Generative Screening of ABX$_3$ Perovskite Compositions for Bandgap-Targeted Materials Discovery
authors: Sunraj Patel, Krishanu Biswas
abstract: Crystal-generation models can explore compositions and atomic arrangements beyond a fixed set of crystal prototypes, but their usefulness for a specific materials family depends on whether the generated structures retain the defining topology and whether their predicted properties remain reliable across the sampled chemistry. Here, a pretrained diffusion model is used to generate candidate ABX$_3$ perovskites and to examine their structural, chemical and electronic-property distributions. A connectivity-based filter distinguishes three-dimensional corner-sharing perovskites from structures that share the same nominal ABX$_3$ stoichiometry. The accepted set contains substantial B-site multiplicity, including ordered double-perovskite configurations that are inaccessible to the two-prototype substitution reference used here. The generated set is enriched in chloride-, bromide- and iodide-containing compositions relative to the Materials Project, while all generated B-site elements are already represented in that database. On the downstream MP-trained ALIGNN scale, the predicted bandgap distribution is shifted towards 1.4 eV, but the target-window fraction (8.2\%) is close to the MP reference fraction (7.3\%); the separate MatterGen and ALIGNN label sources prevent this comparison from establishing target-condition enrichment. An ALIGNN model performs well on a formula-grouped random test split but does not outperform a constant baseline on a deliberately severe B-site-disjoint test. First-principles calculations on six generated structures show that relaxation can alter structural classification and that predicted and calculated gaps can differ appreciably. These results identify both the chemical-space coverage offered by crystal diffusion and the structural and predictive checks needed before its outputs can be treated as materials candidates.

infographic.key_insight: Diffusion generation expands ABX₃ perovskite structural and chemical coverage, but reliable bandgap-targeted discovery requires topology checks and property validation.
infographic.engineering_relevance: For solar-cell materials screening, generated perovskites offer candidate diversity rather than validated absorber performance.
method: Generate ABX₃ candidates with a pretrained crystal diffusion model.
Filter for three-dimensional corner-sharing perovskite connectivity.
Evaluate ALIGNN bandgap predictions and perform first-principles checks on six structures.
infographic.evidence_signal: The generated target-window fraction was 8.2% versus 7.3% for Materials Project, while ALIGNN failed to outperform a constant baseline on a severe B-site-disjoint test.
infographic.watch_item: Different MatterGen and ALIGNN label sources prevent claiming target-condition enrichment; relaxation can change topology, and calculated gaps can differ appreciably from predictions.
infographic.paper_title: Diffusion-Based Generative Screening of ABX$_3$ Perovskite Compositions for Bandgap-Targeted Materials Discovery

title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures
authors: Mahmoud Samadpour, Alireza Fathi Beiraghvandi, Kazem Meraji, Tristan Sachsenweger Ballantyne, Fuxiang Ji, Mahdi Mohammadi
abstract: Surface morphology is widely considered an indicator of thin-film quality, with smoother films generally expected to exhibit more uniform optoelectronic properties. Here, we demonstrate that substantial surface evolution does not necessarily lead to increased electronic heterogeneity in mixed-dimensional perovskite heterostructures. We investigate how low-dimensional Ruddlesden-Popper capping layers derived from the sterically hindered 5-tert-butyl-phenanthridinium cation affect the spatial distributions of photoluminescence (PL) characteristics and quasi-Fermi level splitting (QFLS) in 3D perovskites. By combining statistical atomic force microscopy (AFM) analysis with confocal, spatially resolved PL spectroscopy, we correlate surface topography with microscale optoelectronic properties. Although capping increases surface roughness and height asymmetry, it does not increase electronic inhomogeneity. Instead, the heterostructures exhibit enhanced PL, reduced non-radiative recombination, and improved spatial uniformity of radiative QFLS compared with pristine 3D films. Under accelerated aging, this contrast becomes more pronounced: pristine films develop substantial spatial fluctuations in emission and QFLS, whereas capped heterostructures largely preserve their optoelectronic homogeneity. These findings indicate that the low-dimensional capping layer suppresses aging-induced optoelectronic disorder, demonstrating that electronic uniformity can be maintained despite morphological irregularity. This decoupling provides a design principle for developing durable, high-performance perovskite photovoltaics.

infographic.key_insight: Low-dimensional capping makes 3D perovskite surfaces rougher while improving electronic uniformity, showing that morphological irregularity need not compromise optoelectronic quality.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Mixed-dimensional capping offers a design route toward more durable perovskite photovoltaics by suppressing non-radiative recombination and aging-induced electronic disorder.
method: Form Ruddlesden–Popper capping layers using 5-tert-butyl-phenanthridinium on 3D perovskites.
Combine statistical AFM with spatially resolved confocal photoluminescence spectroscopy.
Compare morphology, emission, and quasi-Fermi level splitting before and after accelerated aging.
infographic.evidence_signal: Despite increased roughness and height asymmetry, capped films show enhanced photoluminescence, more uniform radiative quasi-Fermi level splitting, and better preservation of optoelectronic homogeneity during accelerated aging than pristine films.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative device-efficiency gains or operational lifetime data, so photovoltaic performance benefits remain to be established.
infographic.paper_title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures

title: Nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulation with external field
authors: Chengji Li, Fan Zheng
abstract: Nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulations with classical path approximation (CPA-NAMD) cannot simulate the carrier dynamics under an external field. We develop CPA-NAMD-extF, a first-principles density-matrix framework for calculating field-driven electronic responses along precomputed finite-temperature ionic trajectories. The method combines explicit external-field coupling with self-consistent updates of electronic density while retaining the computational efficiency of the classical-path approximation. Benchmarks against regular TDDFT methods show close agreement for time-dependent dipoles, finite-field currents, and linear optical responses. Applications to the linear absorption spectrum of crystalline and amorphous SiO$_2$ demonstrate its capability to large and structurally complex systems. This method is also applied to the 2D hybrid perovskite $(\mathrm{BA})_2\mathrm{CsPb}_2\mathrm{Br}_7$. Finite-temperature calculations show that the second-order opto-current response is strongly affected by structural fluctuations. Real-space DC current density further reveals pronounced Br-centered vortex currents, and its microscopic origin is investigated.

infographic.key_insight: CPA-NAMD-extF extends classical-path nonadiabatic molecular dynamics to simulate field-driven electronic responses and reveals fluctuation-sensitive opto-currents in a 2D hybrid perovskite.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The method could help analyze finite-temperature photoresponse mechanisms in perovskite solar-cell materials while retaining classical-path computational efficiency.
method: Evolve a first-principles electronic density matrix along precomputed finite-temperature ionic trajectories.
Include explicit external-field coupling and self-consistent electronic-density updates.
Calculate optical responses and resolve real-space DC current density.
infographic.evidence_signal: Benchmarks closely match regular TDDFT for time-dependent dipoles, finite-field currents, and linear optical responses; applications cover crystalline and amorphous SiO₂ and (BA)₂CsPb₂Br₇.
infographic.watch_item: Precomputed ionic trajectories retain the classical-path approximation, so field-induced feedback on ionic motion may require additional treatment.
infographic.paper_title: Nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulation with external field

title: Moiré reconstruction at a twisted SrTiO3 interface
authors: Pengcheng Fei, Meiyu Wang, Suzhen Liu, Zhongwei Zhang, Yang Wu, Bo Hao
abstract: Twisted oxide double layers have emerged as a promising platform for exploring moiré physics, including polar topologies and emergent electronic phases. However, the intrinsic complexity of oxide surfaces, such as contamination, roughness, and the presence of two distinct terminations (AO and BO2), can complicate the identification of buried interfacial structures. Here, using atomically flat SrTiO3 membranes with a predominantly SrO-TiO2 interfacial configuration, we directly visualize a moiré-periodic structural reconstruction at the buried interface that is distinct from the geometric moiré of rigid stacking. The reconstructed interface hosts head-to-head-like polar distortions, moiré-modulated Ti electronic structure, and enhanced microwave admittance in otherwise paraelectric and insulating SrTiO3. Our work demonstrates that, with a well-defined termination, moiré reconstruction could serve as a route to emergent electrical behavior in twisted perovskite oxides.

infographic.key_insight: Twisted SrTiO3 membranes exhibit a reconstructed moiré interface with polar distortions, modified Ti electronic structure, and enhanced microwave admittance.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Controlled interface termination could enable emergent electrical behavior in perovskite oxides, but this study does not demonstrate AI methods or solar-cell performance.
method: Stack atomically flat SrTiO3 membranes with a twist.
Establish a predominantly SrO–TiO2 interfacial configuration.
Directly visualize buried-interface reconstruction and characterize electrical signatures.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports moiré-periodic reconstruction distinct from rigid-stacking geometry, head-to-head-like polar distortions, moiré-modulated Ti electronic structure, and enhanced microwave admittance.
infographic.watch_item: Surface contamination, roughness, and mixed terminations can complicate interface identification and control.
infographic.paper_title: Moiré reconstruction at a twisted SrTiO3 interface

title: Benchmarking Classical Machine Learning Models for Shading-Fault Detection in Rooftop Photovoltaic Systems Using Real Sensor Data
authors: Zablon Ombiro, Bernard Shibwabo
abstract: Most published comparisons of machine-learning classifiers for photovoltaic (PV) fault detection are validated on simulated faults. We compare seven classical and ensemble-tree classifiers on the Réunion dataset, a 4 kW domestic rooftop plant on which shading faults were physically staged and logged. Readings within a staged episode are near-duplicates, so every train/test split is grouped by episode. A 20,800-row subsample that retains all 17 fault episodes was evaluated with three repeats of five-fold group-aware nested cross-validation, with synthetic minority oversampling (SMOTE) applied inside the training folds. Random Forest and XGBoost gave the highest mean accuracy (0.838 and 0.831) and Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC; 0.526 and 0.522). After Holm correction across the 21 pairwise Wilcoxon tests, only Random Forest's accuracy advantage over k-nearest neighbours and the multi-layer perceptron remained significant. Logistic Regression and the Decision Tree (accuracy 0.820) could be separated neither from the ensembles nor from the weakest models. SMOTE lowered binary MCC for six of the seven classifiers. Errors were concentrated in whole episodes: the Random Forest almost entirely missed four of the 17 fault episodes, including one of two uniform-shading and two of five intermittent-shading episodes. A post-hoc diagnostic shows that the no-fault rows were sampled over a wider range of times of day and output levels than the fault rows. Clock time alone reaches an MCC of 0.44, and PV-side voltage alone 0.72. The reported scores therefore reflect operating-condition differences as well as shading signatures. We release the pipeline and the diagnostics, and identify matched no-fault sampling as the step needed before the classifier ranking can be generalised.

infographic.key_insight: Random Forest and XGBoost led shading-fault detection, but operating-condition differences limit conclusions about classifier superiority.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Reliable rooftop PV fault detection requires episode-aware validation and no-fault samples matched to fault operating conditions.
method: Benchmarked seven classifiers on real sensor data from a 4 kW rooftop PV plant with physically staged shading.
Used three repeats of five-fold group-aware nested cross-validation to keep episodes separate.
Applied SMOTE within training folds and Holm correction to pairwise statistical tests.
infographic.evidence_signal: Across 20,800 rows retaining all 17 fault episodes, Random Forest achieved 0.838 accuracy and 0.526 MCC, yet almost entirely missed four fault episodes.
infographic.watch_item: Clock time alone reached 0.44 MCC and PV-side voltage alone 0.72 MCC in post-hoc diagnostics, suggesting operating-condition confounding; matched no-fault sampling is needed before generalising rankings.
infographic.paper_title: Benchmarking Classical Machine Learning Models for Shading-Fault Detection in Rooftop Photovoltaic Systems Using Real Sensor Data

title: The Utility of Physics-Informed Machine Learning in Solar Power Production Forecasting
authors: Peter Pavlík, Franz M. Rohrhofer, Bernhard C. Geiger
abstract: Physics-informed machine learning (PIML) and hybrid modeling have attracted significant attention as approaches for combining physical knowledge with the flexibility of deep learning. In this work, we investigate whether these approaches deliver their commonly claimed benefits for large-scale photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting. We develop two hybrid forecasting architectures that integrate the ADR physical PV efficiency model with the TSMixer neural forecasting architecture through feature augmentation and residual learning. The proposed models are evaluated on a dataset comprising over 3 million samples from 3,713 PV installations across 33 European countries. We assess convergence speed, forecasting accuracy, transferability across geographical regions, and data efficiency. Although the physics-informed models seem to exhibit slightly faster convergence during training, they do not achieve consistent improvements in test-set accuracy, generalization, or performance under limited training data compared to the purely data-driven baseline. These findings suggest that, for modern deep forecasting architectures trained on large datasets, explicitly incorporating the ADR physical model provides limited practical benefit for day-ahead PV forecasting.

infographic.key_insight: Adding ADR-based physical knowledge to TSMixer offered limited practical benefit for day-ahead solar power forecasting compared with a purely data-driven baseline.
infographic.engineering_relevance: For large-scale PV forecasting, added hybrid-model complexity may not deliver reliable gains in accuracy, geographic transferability, or data efficiency.
method: Combine the ADR physical PV efficiency model with TSMixer.
Implement feature-augmentation and residual-learning hybrids.
Compare convergence, accuracy, geographic transferability, and limited-data performance.
infographic.evidence_signal: Evaluation used over 3 million samples from 3,713 PV installations across 33 European countries; hybrids appeared to converge slightly faster but showed no consistent improvements in test accuracy, generalization, or limited-data performance.
infographic.watch_item: The findings concern ADR–TSMixer hybrids for day-ahead forecasting and should not be generalized to all physics-informed models or forecasting settings.
infographic.paper_title: The Utility of Physics-Informed Machine Learning in Solar Power Production Forecasting

title: AutoEnergyDesign: An LLM-Driven Agent for Automatic Energy System Design Optimization
authors: Amedeo Buonanno, Salvatore Fabozzi, Maria Valenti
abstract: Designing building energy systems is a high-dimensional, mixed-integer search problem: when each design is evaluated by a year-long simulation, black-box optimizers typically need hundreds of evaluations. This paper presents AutoEnergyDesign, a framework in which a Large Language Model (LLM) agent reasons over previous simulation results, proposes configuration changes and learns in context from each outcome, while a git-based mechanism automatically reverts unsuccessful changes. The agent couples a reasoning model with an explicit memory organisation (procedural, semantic, episodic and reflective), a constrained action interface and an environment-grounded keep/revert signal. The simulator covers eight technologies (photovoltaics, micro-wind, combined heat and power, solar thermal, gas boilers, batteries, heat pumps and inverters) and computes the 25-year Net Present Cost (NPC), including capital and operating costs and salvage value. On a case study with measured building load profiles, the agent, run with Claude Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 (ten runs of 50 simulations each), is compared with random search, Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) Bayesian optimization and a $(1+1)$ evolution strategy sharing the agent's acceptance rule (300 evaluations, ten seeds). With all three models the agent reaches an NPC of about 3.53 MEUR, 1.20% below the best TPE result and 0.23% below the best evolution-strategy result. It comes within 1% of this design after a median of 18 (Opus) to 27.5 (Haiku) simulations, whereas among the baselines only the evolution strategy does so, in half of its seeds and after a median of 192 evaluations. Opus reaches the best design in all ten runs, Sonnet in six (two runs never come within 1%), and Haiku comes within 1% in every run but reaches it exactly only once. Every decision is recorded in an auditable trace.

infographic.key_insight: AutoEnergyDesign uses an LLM agent to optimize building energy systems—not solar cells—reaching a roughly €3.53 million lifetime cost with fewer simulations than tested conventional optimizers.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The framework could reduce simulation-intensive design effort for systems combining photovoltaics, storage, heating and other energy technologies.
method: Propose configuration changes using simulation history and structured memory.
Evaluate eight technology types through annual simulations and 25-year Net Present Cost.
Keep successful changes and automatically revert unsuccessful ones using git.
infographic.evidence_signal: On one measured-load case study, three LLM variants were tested in ten 50-simulation runs each; the best design cost 1.20% less than the best TPE result and 0.23% less than the best evolution-strategy result.
infographic.watch_item: Results come from a single case study, and reliability varied by LLM; broader validation and accounting for inference costs remain important.
infographic.paper_title: AutoEnergyDesign: An LLM-Driven Agent for Automatic Energy System Design Optimization

title: A Hybrid TFT-NBEATS Framework for Robust Multi-Horizon Photovoltaic Power Forecasting
authors: Shafi Bin Sultan, Sabik Bin Sultan, Mohammad Tajrian Arafat Alvi, Rayhanul Islam Sony, Abdulah Al Numan
abstract: Accurate multi-horizon photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is essential for grid stability, energy scheduling, and the efficient operation of PVbatterygrid systems. However, existing models often fail to jointly capture short-term variability and long-term temporal patterns, while lacking unified multi-horizon capability and interpretability. To address these limitations, this study proposes a novel hybrid deep learning framework that integrates a Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) and N-BEATS within an attention-based fusion architecture. The proposed model leverages TFT to learn short-term temporal dependencies and dynamic feature importance, while N-BEATS captures long-term trend and seasonal components through interpretable basis decomposition. An adaptive attention mechanism dynamically fuses both branches, enabling balanced multi-scale learning. The framework simultaneously generates forecasts for 30-minute, 2-hour, 6-hour, 12-hour, and 24-hour horizons within a single unified pipeline. The model is evaluated using multi-year real-world datasets from the Desert Knowledge Australia Solar Centre (DKASC). Experimental results demonstrate superior performance over statistical, machine learning, and deep learning baselines. The proposed model achieves RMSE values of 42.35, 46.27, 52.29, and 48.11 across the 20162017, 2023, 2024, and 20252026 datasets, respectively, corresponding to a 3540% reduction compared to the best baseline (TFT). Additionally, MAPE remains below 5% across all datasets, indicating high predictive accuracy and stability. The model also provides interpretability through attention visualization and trendseasonality decomposition, and is deployed on a cloud-based platform for real-time forecasting. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework is robust, interpretable, and suitable for practical renewable energy applications.

infographic.key_insight: An attention-fused TFT–N-BEATS model combines short-term dynamics with long-term patterns to forecast photovoltaic power across five horizons.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Unified forecasts from 30 minutes to 24 hours could support grid scheduling and PV–battery operation; this research addresses power forecasting, not solar-cell materials.
method: TFT learns short-term dependencies and dynamic feature importance.
N-BEATS decomposes longer-term trends and seasonality.
Adaptive attention fuses both branches for simultaneous multi-horizon prediction.
infographic.evidence_signal: On multi-year DKASC datasets, the abstract reports RMSE values of 42.35–52.29, a 35–40% reduction versus TFT, and MAPE below 5% across datasets.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract does not specify RMSE units or temporal split details, limiting assessment of practical error magnitude and leakage risk.
infographic.paper_title: A Hybrid TFT-NBEATS Framework for Robust Multi-Horizon Photovoltaic Power Forecasting

title: Ammonium thiocyanate enables in-situ structural templating of MAPbI3 via quasi-2D perovskite scaffold
authors: Sophie Tucker, Isaac Metcalf, Rachel C. Kilbride, Elena J. Cassella, Jessica H. Persaud, Faiz Mandani
abstract: Ammonium thiocyanate (NH4SCN) has been used extensively to improve the current extraction and device performance of quasi-two-dimensional perovskite solar cells. Whilst this additive has been shown to influence quasi-2D perovskite crystallisation, a detailed understanding of its mechanism has not yet been established. Through spectroscopic and structural studies, we demonstrate that NH4SCN enables quasi-2D perovskite phases to structurally template the dominant 3D phase. Contrary to previous reports, we suggest that the benefit of this additive comes from an improvement to the 3D perovskite structure, not from charges transferring through vertically oriented 2D perovskite layers. We show that this additive provides kinetic control over the quasi-2D phase formation, suppressing the unfavourable n = 1 perovskite phase and promoting the growth of high-n 2D scaffold phases by extending the nucleation window. This promotes the in-situ templated growth of MAPbI3. We provide robust structural analysis demonstrating highly (110)-ordered 3D perovskite, with the mechanism confirmed by close lattice matching between this phase and quasi-2D phases. Furthermore, we show that this structural control is cation dependent, requiring both close lattice matching between quasi-2D and 3D perovskite phases, and successful kinetic control of the relevant quasi-2D phases.

infographic.key_insight: NH4SCN promotes high-n quasi-2D scaffold phases that template highly (110)-ordered 3D MAPbI3, rather than primarily enabling charge transport through vertically oriented 2D layers.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Controlling crystallisation kinetics and lattice matching offers a route to improve perovskite film structure for solar cells.
method: Use spectroscopic and structural studies to probe NH4SCN-mediated crystallisation.
Extend the nucleation window to suppress n = 1 phases and promote high-n quasi-2D scaffolds.
Assess lattice matching and cation dependence of quasi-2D-to-3D templating.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports structural evidence of highly (110)-ordered MAPbI3 and close lattice matching with quasi-2D phases, but gives no quantitative device-performance results.
infographic.watch_item: The templating mechanism is cation dependent and requires both compatible lattice matching and effective kinetic control.
infographic.paper_title: Ammonium thiocyanate enables in-situ structural templating of MAPbI3 via quasi-2D perovskite scaffold

title: Temperature-Dependent Raman Signatures of Local Symmetry Breaking in Vacancy Double Perovskite Cs$_2$SnI$_6$
authors: Tomke E. Glier, Nicholas J. Weadock, Julian A. Vigil, Cole Shank, Xixi Qin, Gabriel J. Graf
abstract: Understanding and controlling the optical, thermal and mechanical properties of K$_2$PtCl$_6$-type double perovskites is essential for the design of lead-free, high-performance thermoelectric and optoelectronic materials. In this study, we investigate Cs$_2$SnI$_6$ using temperature-dependent near-resonance Raman scattering, complemented by density functional theory-based phonon calculations. The appearance of Raman-forbidden phonon modes in the Raman response at cryogenic temperatures provides strong evidence for local symmetry breaking that does not develop into a global structural phase transition. Through detailed analysis of phonon intensities, energies, and spectral lineshapes, we characterize the temperature evolution of the symmetry-broken structural response of Cs$_2$SnI$_6$. Below 200 K, multi-phonon scattering is strongly enhanced, and symmetry-forbidden Raman modes emerge. The temperature dependence of phonon intensities follows a phenomenological Arrhenius behavior, revealing an activation energy of 15-20 meV. These results establish temperature-dependent Raman spectroscopy as a sensitive probe of local structural distortions and anharmonic structural dynamics in Cs$_2$SnI$_6$, providing a robust experimental basis for discussing the microscopic origins of symmetry breaking and electron-phonon coupling in halide double perovskites.

infographic.key_insight: Cryogenic Raman spectra reveal local symmetry breaking in Cs₂SnI₆ without a global structural phase transition.
infographic.engineering_relevance: These structural insights could inform lead-free optoelectronic material design, but the study does not demonstrate solar-cell performance gains or use AI.
method: Temperature-dependent near-resonance Raman spectroscopy
DFT-based phonon calculations
Analysis of phonon intensities, energies, and lineshapes
infographic.evidence_signal: Below 200 K, enhanced multiphonon scattering and Raman-forbidden modes appear, while phonon intensities show phenomenological Arrhenius behavior with a 15–20 meV activation energy.
infographic.watch_item: Cryogenic spectroscopic signatures alone do not establish the microscopic distortion mechanism or its impact on operating solar cells.
infographic.paper_title: Temperature-Dependent Raman Signatures of Local Symmetry Breaking in Vacancy Double Perovskite Cs$_2$SnI$_6$

title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites
authors: Mahesh Eledath-Changarath, Jesús Ortiga-Fibla, Andrés F. Gualdrón-Reyes, Jesús Rodríguez-Romero, Iván Mora-Seró, Ana Cros
abstract: Long-term stability remains a critical challenge limiting the photovoltaic and optoelectronic applications of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites. In these materials, the choice of the organic spacer plays a key role not only in enhancing environmental stability, but also in determining their structural characteristics and carrier dynamics. Here, we present an environmental photo- and thermal-stability analysis of BA2PbI4 and PEA2PbI4 two-dimensional lead halide perovskites by means of confocal micro-Raman and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy techniques. We have investigated two different organic spacers, n-butylammonium (BA) and 2-phenylethylammonium (PEA), which provide comparable room-temperature luminescence in freshly exfoliated perovskite nanoflakes and degrade similarly through the removal of organic components and fast crystal phase decomposition into PbI2 and Pb0. However, we observed that the PEA organic cation significantly improves crystal morphology and suppresses lattice defects, resulting in slower degradation and enhanced resistance to light and thermal stress under ambient conditions. Our findings indicate that structural and chemical engineering, along with surface passivation and encapsulation strategies, are essential for achieving long-term stability in two-dimensional halide perovskite devices. Nevertheless, optimizing the balance between stability and device performance remains a critical consideration.

infographic.key_insight: PEA organic spacers improve morphology and suppress lattice defects in two-dimensional lead iodide perovskites, slowing degradation relative to BA spacers under ambient light and thermal stress.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Spacer selection can improve perovskite durability, but practical devices also require structural and chemical engineering, surface passivation, and encapsulation.
method: Compared BA2PbI4 and PEA2PbI4 perovskite nanoflakes.
Assessed light and thermal stability under ambient conditions.
Probed degradation using confocal micro-Raman and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy.
infographic.evidence_signal: Freshly exfoliated samples showed comparable room-temperature luminescence, while PEA-based crystals degraded more slowly despite both materials losing organic components and decomposing into PbI2 and metallic Pb.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative stability gains or device-level efficiency tests, so improved material durability should not be equated with proven solar-cell performance.
infographic.paper_title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites

title: Unifying Low-Frequency Raman and Infrared Signatures across Perovskites
authors: Ethan Berger, Erik Fransson, Apinya Ngoipala, Lucas Svensson, Priyanka Deswal, Mehmet Baskurt
abstract: Perovskites have been studied for a wide range of applications, from oxide-based ferroelectrics to halide-perovskite photovoltaics. Despite their diverse functionalities, these materials share strong lattice anharmonicity arising from structural instabilities such as polar off-centering and octahedral tilting. These anharmonic distortions strongly influence the low-frequency vibrational response and can be observed in infrared (IR) and Raman spectra. However, low-frequency IR and Raman signatures are typically investigated separately, hindering the development of a unified understanding of vibrational spectroscopy across perovskite classes. In this work, we use machine-learning-based molecular dynamics to simulate the IR and Raman spectra of oxide perovskites (SrTiO$_3$ and BaTiO$_3$), halide perovskites (CsPbBr$_3$, CsSnBr$_3$, and CsGeBr$_3$) and double halide perovskites (Cs$_2$AgAlBr$_6$ and Cs$_2$AgBiBr$_6$). By comparing materials exhibiting polar, tilt-driven and mixed instabilities, we find that polar off-centering leads to enhanced low-frequency IR and dielectric responses, whereas nonpolar modes, particularly octahedral tilting, are associated with Raman central peaks. The strength of the low-frequency features also depends on how strongly the underlying modes couple to polarization or dielectric susceptibility. Finally, we show that the dynamics of these instabilities play an important role, with slow polar reorientations shifting the dielectric response to very low frequencies and overdamped tilting modes producing persistent Raman central peaks. These results establish a unified framework connecting low-frequency IR and Raman spectra to the symmetry, coupling and dynamics of their underlying anharmonic lattice instabilities.

infographic.key_insight: Across perovskites, polar off-centering enhances low-frequency infrared and dielectric responses, while nonpolar octahedral tilting is associated with Raman central peaks.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Linking spectral features to lattice instabilities can guide interpretation of structural dynamics in halide-perovskite solar-cell materials.
method: Simulate infrared and Raman spectra using machine-learning-based molecular dynamics.
Compare seven oxide, halide and double-halide perovskites with polar, tilt-driven or mixed instabilities.
Relate spectral signatures to mode symmetry, coupling strength and dynamics.
infographic.evidence_signal: Simulations across seven perovskites link slow polar reorientations to very-low-frequency dielectric responses and overdamped tilting modes to persistent Raman central peaks.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract reports no solar-cell device tests or quantitative experimental validation, so photovoltaic performance implications remain unestablished.
infographic.paper_title: Unifying Low-Frequency Raman and Infrared Signatures across Perovskites
